acceptance: Red first: with remote.origin.fetch narrowed so it omits main, SyncToOrigin still sees the new origin/main; red on main
No production call outside internal/mainsync runs a bare fetch of origin main (a structure test)
100% coverage on each changed function, zero code comments, and the integration and mainsync package notes in STE
fix: Route SyncToOrigin through mainsync (or at least its fetch helper with the explicit refspec), so the train and the plane read the same origin/main. Red test first: a fetch config that omits main still refreshes origin/main for the train.
summary: PR #1616 made go/internal/mainsync the one home of fetch-classify-fast-forward and its explicit refspec +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main; the ship window and the wave boundary both call it. go/internal/integration/sync.go SyncToOrigin still runs git fetch origin main, which leaves refs/remotes/origin/main stale when remote.origin.fetch is narrowed or unset (proven by the #1616 architecture review probe). The internal-mainsync package note's one-home claim is therefore not yet true for the integration train.
title: integration.SyncToOrigin still runs a plain fetch origin main, a fourth copy of the fetch rule that can leave origin/main stale
